title: Chain-map representatives of affine strictly perfect derived arrows
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an affine open, and $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ strictly perfect complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every arrow $f:Q(A^\bullet)\to Q(B^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a chain map $\alpha:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ such that $Q(\alpha)=f$.

proof.text: Use affine_perfect_module_model on A and B to obtain actual complexes P and T, a proof that P is K-projective, and complex isomorphisms eA:F(P)~A and eB:F(T)~B. These module models are proved by actual termwise global sections, not chosen as data of a definition.

Obtain the full derived sheafification G and comparison c:Q followed by G ~ F followed by Q. Form a=c(P) followed by Q(eA) and b=c(T) followed by Q(eB). Fullness gives g with G(g)=a.hom followed by f followed by b.inv. Apply CochainComplex.IsKProjective.exists_Q_map_eq from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.KProjective to obtain beta:P->T with Q(beta)=g.

Define alpha=eA.inv followed by F(beta) followed by eB.hom. Naturality of c identifies Q(F(beta)) with c(P).inv followed by G(g) followed by c(T).hom. Substitute the fullness equation and cancel the comparison and complex isomorphisms. Functor.map_comp, associativity and the iso cancellation identities prove Q(alpha)=f.
